title: What people frame, v
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Valentine's. A man wants a photo of a woman framed and asks for the cheapest frame. Wood gives him the second cheapest and charges him for the cheapest. The Owner sees.

panels.composition: The counter. A MAN, young, nervous, with a snapshot. The Owner at the back.

balloons.text: Cheapest one you got. It's — it's just a snapshot.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a nervous young man at a frame-shop counter holding a snapshot, a young clerk, an older woman at the back

panels.composition: The snapshot: a woman laughing, out of focus, the kind of picture you keep anyway.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, close-up of a slightly out-of-focus snapshot of a woman laughing

panels.composition: Wood taking the second-cheapest frame off the wall — the black one with the bevel — and ringing up the cheapest. The Owner's glasses come up.

balloons.text: Sign said fifteen for that one.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, a young clerk handing over a black beveled frame while ringing up a lower price, an older woman looking up over her reading glasses from the back

panels.composition: After. The Owner, beside him, tapping the register.
panels.caption: Wednesday.

image.prompt: brush-pen over blue pencil, xerox grain, stark black spotting, an older woman tapping a register beside a young clerk, saying something short
